page.overview:
What is Flying Dutchman?

The Flying Dutchman is a legendary ship from maritime folklore, and is largely infamous as a ghost ship. It is the main vessel of the Flying Pirates and was once captained by the original Vander Decken and his descendants, up until Vander Decken IX.

The Flying Dutchman resembles the stereotypical representation of a ghost ship: old and worn from time. The sails are torn and tattered, moss and barnacles are growing out from various spots of the ship, and the mast is similar to a clock tower in design. On the bottom front sail is the name "FLYING DUTCHMAN", and the top one bears the crew's Jolly Roger, a fanged skull with cutlasses, their blades pointing down in place of crossbones. The ship's figurehead bears the same skull and swords. The Flying Dutchman is a large ship, being as large as Wadatsumi, a fish-man who dwarfs even Shirahoshi.

The ship is not coated with resin since the crew can survive the underwater environment due to being fish-men. The vessel can also withstand the underwater pressure of 10000 feet below sea level due to already being full of holes that equalize the water pressure inside and outside the hull. Only a small portion on the deck is coated for their captain to reside in (as the current holder of the title, though being a fish-man, ate a Devil Fruit).

The Flying Dutchman is described as a ship that is unable to make port, and must wander the endless sea forever. This was due to the ship's deranged captain Vander Decken committing atrocious crimes. As a result, he brought about God's wrath, who then punished him by cursing both him and the ship. It is a bad omen when the ship does appear.
